observation.visible_scene: A clear glass tumbler heaped with a mound of white crushed-ice/snow sits centered on a dark, glossy, wet-looking surface, with a faint haze/vapor drifting around the cup. In the upper-right corner a person's thumb and fingers hold a dark cylindrical nozzle or can pointed downward toward the ice.
visible_changes: For the first ~0.5 s the scene is essentially static: the ice mound, the held nozzle, and the surface show no change.

From about t=0.56 s a thin stream/spray begins to descend from the held nozzle onto the ice, initially faint, then appearing as a narrow vertical line and at times as a short white blurred column (e.g. t=1.28 s).
The pouring stream continues intermittently (clearly visible around t=0.8–1.2 s, t=1.6–2.0 s, t=2.1–2.3 s, t=2.6–2.7 s) and is no longer visible after roughly t=2.8 s.
The shape of the ice mound changes over the clip: the right-side peak present early on lowers/settles, and by the later frames a small distinct ice chunk protrudes from the top-right of the mound.
The held nozzle and the fingers gradually move out of the top-right of the frame as the clip progresses.
The framing shifts slightly (the cup appears a touch larger and repositioned), indicating a small camera drift/zoom rather than movement of the cup itself.
outside_clip_unknowns: The identity of the substance being dispensed and whether it is a pour or a spray.
The cause of the ice-mound shape change (melting, settling, or added material is not determinable).
What preceded the first visible stream and what follows after the stream stops (both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries).
uncertain_details: Whether the apparent change in ice shape is physical deformation or partly a viewing/camera effect.
The exact start and end moments of the stream, since it fades in and out between frames.
The distinction between camera motion and slight repositioning of the held nozzle.
